title: HBM3E memory controller: sideband-ECC controller (256 page entries {channel haddr[10:8], pc/bank haddr[15:11]}, row = haddr[31:18], storage = 256 columns per channel, each word with 5 SEC check bits carried on ecc); the TB flips bits of stored codewords in its DRAM model and the reads must still return the written data; line commands (RDL / WRL: BL8 with dqs and per-beat ECC) and an MR file (CL / CWL)

regs.name: CMD
regs.desc: Host command beat; writing CMD2 sends it: a command (the core takes it when it is idle and no refresh is due), or one of the 8 data beats that follow a WRL

fdesc.hcmd: 1 ACT, 2 RD, 3 WR, 4 PRE, 5 RDL, 6 WRL (then 8 data beats), 7 MR access; 0 is a no-op; ignored on a data beat
fdesc.haddr: host address (bank, row and column fields below); MR access: [3] 1 MRR / 0 MRW, [2:0] MR index
fdesc.hwdata: word to write (WR), MRW value (bits 7:0), or a WRL data beat (beat 0 = column {haddr[7:3], 0})

fields.desc: word of the last RD (or word 7 of an RDL, {8'h0, MR} of an MRR), valid once DONE is set

regs.name: RLINE
regs.desc: Line of the last RDL (RLINE0 = bits 31:0)

fields.desc: the 8 words of the last RDL (word k = column {haddr[7:3], k} in bits 16k+15:16k), held until the next RDL

irqs.name: DONE
irqs.desc: a RD, RDL or MRR finished; RDATA (and RLINE for an RDL) holds its data

notes: ck_t, ck_c, cke, cs_n, act_n, ba, addr, ras_n, cas_n, we_n, dq, ecc and dqs are the DRAM pins and trace_valid, trace_cmd and trace_addr the command trace (one clock before each command on the pins); they pass through unchanged.

Address map and behaviour of the core: sideband-ECC controller (256 page entries {channel haddr[10:8], pc/bank haddr[15:11]}, row = haddr[31:18], storage = 256 columns per channel, each word with 5 SEC check bits carried on ecc); the TB flips bits of stored codewords in its DRAM model and the reads must still return the written data.
A line is the 8 columns {haddr[7:3], k}. CL = 5 + MR0[3:0], CWL = 5 + MR1[3:0]; each line beat carries its own 5 SEC check bits on ecc and is corrected on the way in.
The core's own verification (pin-level checker, 100% coverage) is tb/cov/HBM3E_sva.sv with tb/HBM3E_tb.sv; this wrapper test drives the core only through the registers.
